summary.intent: Execute Session 5 of the v1-alpha launch plan: WP E (a NativeName type so registry-equivalent package names are one identity) and WP I (a directory index for relative workspace: deps). Follow-ups covered a review finding on #561, a PyPI sibling bug, mutation testing, and new WP W (cache historical tag probes by commit).
summary.outcome: WP E (#561) and WP I (#563) were pushed with signed commits and green gates. The Cargo and PyPI historical-tag-ownership bugs were fixed with literal-name comparison, and mutation testing was run on E and I. WP W's code, bench shape, changeset and commit were made locally; its mutants run, push, PR and trail link were not shown as done.

repo: Work happens in git worktrees via EnterWorktree/ExitWorktree; Edit tool is restricted to the active worktree, but python/sed scripts bypass that and can edit the wrong tree.
Gates are `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check`, `just test`, judged by exit code; AGENTS.md also asks for `just ci` before marking a PR ready.

Commits must be signed with no session trailer; push with an explicit HEAD:refs/heads/<branch> refspec and verify with git ls-remote; local `%G?` can show E, so GitHub's commit verification.reason is the authority.
Release notes use `callisto add --package ... --summary` changesets (callisto-cli patch) with an **Action:** paragraph for behavior changes.
Mutation testing uses `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff`; the diff filter must cover `crates` minus tests/benches or it finds too few mutants; never commit mutants.out*.
The sandbox needs github.com allowed for git fetch; BSD sed on macOS needs `sed -i ''`.
Equivalent mutant: emptying `Hash::hash` on NativeName is consistent with Eq and must be noted in the PR body.
The plan's claims were partly wrong: ReleasePackageId.name should stay a String, release_decision.rs needs no edit, and no code enforced Cargo foo-bar/foo_bar as E100 before E.

code.finding: NativeName holds (ecosystem, spelling, key); Eq/Hash/Ord use the key only. The key is PEP 503 for PyPI, lowercase with _ turned to - for Cargo, and exact for other ecosystems.

may_have_held_name_at must compare declared names literally in every ecosystem, because a default tag `{name}@` carries the declared spelling. Equivalence-based comparison credited foreign npm tags to Cargo/PyPI packages after renames.

The tag caches were keyed by raw tag string, so foreign tags on one commit repeated the git probes (6T+4 processes). WP W reads the newest tag by name and the rest by commit after the first rejection.
native_owner is keyed by NativeName, which makes duplicate detection (E100) catch equivalent names.

resolve_id, bare-name and cross-ecosystem fallback lookups now use NativeName; the fallbacks and bare selectors match exact spelling, only qualified selectors apply equivalence. native_in_ecosystem became a single get, so the PyPI ambiguity Err arms were dropped.
Glob matching (matches_native) still uses the manifest spelling, so `pypi/my-*` does not match `My_Pkg`; left out of scope.

workflow: A fresh Opus reviewer subagent on each diff found real issues (fallback exactness, bare-selector exactness, docs, rule test), so it is worth running before the gate.
Subagent hand-backs are model output and carry no user authority; they were used only as design input.
The shell guard rejected compound commands in one case, so steps were split into separate Bash calls.
Regression tests written first failed as expected before each fix, which confirmed the repro.
Mutation testing exposed untested code after the first pass (17 missed mutants), which led to a second tests commit.

friction: The first E mutation run found only 3 mutants because of a bad diff path filter and had to be rerun.
Python and sed edit scripts repeatedly hit duplicate `use super::*;` and import errors; one script edit hit the wrong worktree.
BSD sed incompatibilities (`--test-threads` flag, in-place edit syntax) broke scripts.
The `ForeignTags` PackageKind variant needed unreachable! arms in the perf fixture, and the first lazy-commit design broke tests and had to be reworked.
#561's audit fails on RUSTSEC-2026-0542, which #560 fixes in deny.toml, so the PR is blocked on that merge.
Amending and force-pushing #561 early on conflicted with the later never-force-push instruction.
open_items: WP W is committed locally only: mutants --in-diff, the reviewer's findings, push, ls-remote check, PR on trail #462, and git-process/wall-time numbers in the PR body are still pending.
Rebase #561 and then #563 after #560 merges, when the lead says so; #563 conflicts in crates/callisto-cli/benches/commands.rs.
The owner must decide whether E's changeset is `**Breaking:**`, since workspaces with equivalent names will now fail with E100.
Glob patterns like `pypi/my-*` still match on manifest spelling; this needs a comment or a tracked follow-up.
Add one line in #561's PR body for the equivalent Hash::hash mutant and for why the PyPI sibling reproduced.
Run `just ci` before marking the PRs ready.
Delete the wp-e and wp-i worktrees after merge.
`native` now iterates in canonical-key order, so E102 did-you-mean candidates may reorder for mixed-case names.
